body.heading: Progress you can see
paragraphs: Big efforts — learning a language, getting stronger, saving money — improve in increments too small to feel day by day. If the only success that counts is the final one, months of real progress can feel like nothing.

Keeping a simple record changes that. A line in a notebook, a chart on the wall, a list of finished pieces: visible evidence that effort is accumulating, even when the mirror or the score has not caught up yet.

body.heading: Collect wins on purpose
paragraphs: End the day by naming one small win, however ordinary: the email sent, the page read, the ten minutes practised. It takes thirty seconds and quietly rewires what you pay attention to.
On hard days the win might be “I rested” or “I asked for help.” Those count too. A practice that only celebrates perfect days will not survive real life.

takeaway: Write down one small win a day, and watch what it does over a month.
